newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL secondaries end at new high, blue chips off.
newsitem.headline: KL secondaries end at new high, blue chips off.

text.p: Malaysian Second Board stocks surged 3.10 percent to a new closing high on Tuesday, helped by a continued dose of retail-led buying as blue chips continued to flounder despite a positive trade report.
The Second Board index jumped 16.13 points to 537.12, eclipsing its previous closing high of 520.99 set on Monday.

But investor disinterest kept larger counters in the doldrums, with the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange Composite Index easing 2.92 points to 1,113.45. Early in the day, the market was pleasantly surprised with news of a 574.1 million ringgit trade surplus in June.
The trade surplus in June followed a 238.5 million ringgit gain in May and dispelled rumours of a deficit.
Still, the major stocks were uninspired by the news. "Sentiment is neither here nor there, so people take good news in a rather blase manner," said one market analyst with a local firm.
Among gainers in the Second Board sector, MESB Bhd rose 3.70 to 15.30 ringgit, Ho Wah Genting added 3.10 to 16.30 ringgit and Prolexus rose 1.40 to 8.80 ringgit.
Volume totalled over 171 million shares, and losers led gainers by 294 to 260.
